reviewers.summary: In-process extraction meets the input byte and page checks, but an under-limit compressed PDF can still exhaust API process memory during page text extraction.

findingList.message: The byte and page caps do not bound decompression or extracted text. This leaves the API process exposed to resource exhaustion from a small compressed PDF (OWASP A10:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: ParseCore checks the compressed input size and page count, then calls page.Text in the API process without a bound on decompressed stream size or extracted text.
evidence.failureScenario: A PDF under the 10 MB limit with a Flate stream that expands to hundreds of megabytes reaches page.Text. PdfPig can allocate that expanded content in the API process, exhausting its memory and disrupting the service. The updated FlateBomb test pads the fixture above 10 MB, so it rejects the input before exercising this path.

reviewers.summary: The new tests cover the listed fixture outcomes and malformed-document behavior. The 201-page limit test does not verify the criterion that zero pages are extracted.

findingList.message: The 201-page case does not prove extraction stops before reading page text. Add an observable seam or assertion that fails if any page text is accessed.

evidence.codePathTraced: PdfLimitsAreCheckedBeforeParsing counts calls to openDocument and asserts the returned state and empty text for a 201-page PDF, but it does not observe whether page text was extracted.
evidence.failureScenario: If the parser extracts text from all 201 pages and then returns RejectedRetryable with empty text, the test still passes even though the criterion requires zero pages to be extracted.

reviewers.summary: The change enforces the document byte and page-count caps, but a PDF within both limits can still expand to unbounded page text during in-process extraction and exhaust API resources.

findingList.message: OWASP A06:2025 (Insecure Design): in-process extraction does not bound decompressed page content or extraction work, so a small compressed PDF can exhaust API resources.

evidence.codePathTraced: A submitted PDF passes the 10 MB input-size check and page-count check, then PdfPig extracts each page's text directly in the API process at page.Text. The extraction has no decompressed-content, memory, or time bound.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits a PDF under 10 MB with one compressed content stream that expands to an enormous amount of text. PdfPig materializes that text in the API process, exhausting its memory or CPU and disrupting service before the parser can return a result.
